title: Compare Historical Volatility Estimators
concept: realized volatility, overnight returns and annualisation
description: Use one synthetic OHLC sample to explain why five realized-volatility estimates differ; this is not implied-volatility inversion.
objective: Reproduce all five estimates on the same sessions, audit overnight risk and state the annualisation convention.
marketData: Original synthetic OHLC example; not live or observed market data
Unadjusted hypothetical prices; no corporate action implied
steps: Use the CSV in the Python starter; the first row supplies the previous close.
Compute close-to-close sample variance with denominator n−1. Compare Parkinson, Garman-Klass and Rogers-Satchell over the same 11 sessions.
Add overnight variance in Yang-Zhang and explain why a range estimator can miss gap risk.
Change only annualisation from 252 to 365. Explain the sqrt(365/252) change; do not call it a change in observed daily variance.
Use the Realized Volatility Lab synthetic example to check your numbers, export the evidence and state why none of these is a market implied-volatility quote.
hints: All estimators must share the same session set, rows 1..N−1.
Sample variances center returns and use n−1; range contributions are averaged over n.
Do not mix adjusted closes with unadjusted OHLC ranges. A calendar gap is a data-quality fact to inspect, not an automatic zero return.

import csv, io, json
from math import log, sqrt
from statistics import mean, variance

CSV = """date,open,high,low,close
2024-01-02,100.00,101.40,99.35,100.90
2024-01-03,101.05,102.10,100.20,101.55
2024-01-04,101.40,102.00,99.80,100.15
2024-01-05,100.25,101.65,99.90,101.20
2024-01-08,101.45,102.80,100.95,102.35
2024-01-09,102.20,103.10,101.20,101.75
2024-01-10,101.60,102.45,100.70,101.10
2024-01-11,101.35,103.00,101.05,102.70
2024-01-12,102.55,103.25,101.70,102.05
2024-01-15,102.20,103.60,101.85,103.10
2024-01-16,103.00,104.10,102.35,103.75
2024-01-17,103.90,104.45,102.70,103.05
"""
rows = [{k: (v if k == "date" else float(v)) for k,v in row.items()} for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(CSV))]
sessions = [(previous, row) for previous, row in zip(rows, rows[1:])]
# The first row anchors the previous close; every estimator uses the same 11 sessions.
close = [log(row["close"] / previous["close"]) for previous,row in sessions]
overnight = [log(row["open"] / previous["close"]) for previous,row in sessions]
open_close = [log(row["close"] / row["open"]) for previous,row in sessions]
high_low = [log(row["high"] / row["low"]) for previous,row in sessions]
rs = mean(log(row["high"]/row["open"])*log(row["high"]/row["close"]) + log(row["low"]/row["open"])*log(row["low"]/row["close"]) for _,row in sessions)
n = len(sessions)
k = 0.34 / (1.34 + (n+1)/(n-1))
variances = {
    "closeToClose": variance(close),
    "parkinson": mean(x*x for x in high_low)/(4*log(2)),
    "garmanKlass": mean(0.5*h*h - (2*log(2)-1)*c*c for h,c in zip(high_low,open_close)),
    "rogersSatchell": rs,
    "yangZhang": variance(overnight) + k*variance(open_close) + (1-k)*rs,
}
annualized = {name: sqrt(252*max(0,value)) for name,value in variances.items()}
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(json.dumps({"sessions": n, "annualization": 252, "annualizedVolatility": annualized}, indent=2))
